LEARNING PATH · CLASS 40 · HEALTHY FOOD & EATING WELL · AGES 4–5

Healthy Food & Eating Well — twenty-one happy food habits.

Twenty-one printable food cards for ages four to five, in three shelves: what’s on the plate, meals & drinks, and how we eat. Every card wears one big food habit in words YOU can say back — and every card turns the habit into tonight’s job, right here. It all starts with the smiling cover apple: healthy food is not a lecture, it is a plate YOU are proud of.

Start with the Balanced Plate →Back to the Learning Path ↗
HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

One habit. The child says it. Then the plate does the teaching.

These cards carry no lectures — each one prints a single big habit: the balanced plate, chewing well, trying new foods, sitting down, washing hands first. The short pages turn every title into YOUR own sentence and add one thing to try tonight that takes less than a minute to set up: two breakfast options laid out at bedtime, a tummy check halfway through dinner, one brave no-thank-you bite of something new. Food habits grow the same way the cards run — small, happy and repeated.

The shelves follow the meal. The plate shelf names the food groups you actually see — fruit, vegetables, dairy, protein, whole grains — and the rainbow rule that paints them. The meals shelf walks YOUR day: breakfast, lunch, dinner, the healthy snack in between, water to drink and clean hands first. The habits shelf is how the table works: sit down, eat slowly, chew well, try new foods, notice full, eat together, make the healthy choice, feel the energy.

AROUND THE SCHOOL

Where the food learning grows.

Name the fruits & vegetables in Class 22 · Ages 3–5 ↗Everyday habits in Class 32 · Ages 4–5 ↗The Cafeteria’s sixty-two food cards · Ages 2–5 ↗The parents’ shelf in the library · All 21 cards to print ↗

Class 22 names the fruits and vegetables this class serves; Class 32 builds the hand-washing and helping habits this table runs on; and the school’s Cafeteria room keeps sixty-two food cards with their own activities — every tray food named, counted and pointed at. Naming here, tasting there: the shelves finish each other. And when the cards need printing, parents will find the whole deck on the parents’ shelf in the flashcards library — download and print buttons under every card, no extra pages to hop through.

A plate YOU helped build is a plate YOU will eat. Every card here hands the habit to you — the choosing, the washing, the trying — and your grown-up’s whole job is to keep the options worthy of a yes.
